title: Second-Order SQL Injection via Stored Username
learning_objectives: Distinguish a safe parameterised INSERT from an unsafe raw query that re-uses stored input
Recognise a second-order SQL injection where the sink is far from the source
Balance quotes and comments so a payload stores cleanly yet re-splices as valid SQL
Craft a UNION SELECT that matches the referrals column count to exfiltrate a secret column
flag_hint: /solve compares ?secret to the admin account's per-container session_secret; on match it returns the flag from the flag file.
inspired_by: Second-order (stored) SQL injection family — OWASP WSTG-INPV-05, PortSwigger stored/second-order SQLi write-ups
